questions.q: Per this lesson, how is a user's effective object/field access calculated?
options: The most restrictive source wins
The most recently assigned source wins
It's the union of the profile plus every assigned permission set, direct or via group
Only the profile matters; permission sets are advisory
questions.explain: Effective access is the union of every applicable source — profile, direct permission sets, and permission sets inside assigned groups.

questions.q: Can a permission set remove a permission that a user's profile already grants?
options: Yes, using the Deny checkbox
No -- neither profiles nor permission sets have a deny/remove setting for object or field permissions
Yes, but only for custom fields
Yes, if it's assigned after the profile
questions.explain: The lesson states explicitly that neither profiles nor permission sets can subtract access — only the absence of any grant results in no access.

questions.q: What is the fastest reliable way to check a user's actual combined CRUD access to an object, per this lesson?
options: Manually add up every profile and permission set by memory
Object Manager's Object Access tab, switching between Permission Sets, Permission Set Groups, and Profiles sub-tabs
The Role Hierarchy setup page
The organization-wide default settings page
questions.explain: The lesson recommends Object Manager's Object Access tab as the reliable source of truth instead of guessing by hand.

questions.q: A user's profile is silent on Edit access to a field, but a permission set assigned to them grants Edit. What's their effective access?
options: No Edit access, because the profile takes precedence
Edit access, because any one grant from any one source is enough
It depends on which was assigned first
Edit access only during business hours
questions.explain: Per the union rule, any single grant from profile or permission set gives the user that access overall.

questions.q: What changes mathematically when three individually-assigned permission sets are bundled into one Permission Set Group instead?
options: Nothing about the resulting access -- it's the same union, just assignable as one unit
The user gains access to additional objects the sets never granted
The permissions become mutually exclusive instead of additive
The group automatically adds Modify All on every object
questions.explain: The lesson's worked example shows grouping doesn't change the math -- it's identical union, just packaged for one-click assignment.
